commitResults.messageTitle: Level-0: Rename Computa and add greeting
Level-1: Echo commands and exit on bye
Level-4: Add todos deadlines and events
Level-5: Handle invalid input with exceptions
Level-6: Delete tasks with ArrayList storage
Docs: Document Computa features and testing
Add Storage class and initialise data file
Implement Level-8 date and time support
commitResults.messageBody: Parse supported date and date-time inputs into java.time values, format them for display, and add an on-date query for deadlines and events. Reject impossible or reversed date ranges and skip invalid persisted records. Extend the UI plan and README to document the new behavior.

Move greeting, separators, task display, acknowledgements, farewell, and error output into Ui. Keep Computa focused on coordinating input, task operations, and persistence while preserving the existing console transcript. Document the new class in the project structure.

Add the abstract Command contract, Parser recognition, and ExitCommand implementation. Route the bye command through Parser, Command, and Ui while retaining the existing handling for all other commands. This establishes the stretch-goal architecture without changing user-visible behavior.

Keep src/main/java as the source root while separating the application, commands, tasks, storage, UI, utilities, and exceptions into cohesive computa packages. Update imports, launch/build commands, README structure, and the UI test plan so packaged classes compile and run consistently.

Adapt the imported Gradle support to the packaged Computa application, target Java 25, produce computa.jar, and preserve UTF-8 output when running through Gradle. Document wrapper build and run commands while leaving JUnit execution for the A-JUnit increment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add high-value JUnit coverage for parser and storage
commitResults.messageBody: Cover supported and invalid date inputs, display and storage formatting, task persistence, missing files, and corrupted records. Document the approximately 50 percent high-value coverage target and require tests to stay current after code changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Package Computa as an executable fat JAR
commitResults.messageBody: Configure Shadow to set the Computa entry point and produce computa.jar as part of the normal build lifecycle. Document how to create, locate, run, and distribute the generated JAR without committing build artifacts.

commitResults.messageTitle: Select Java 25 toolchain for JAR builds
commitResults.messageBody: Ensure Gradle selects the installed Java 25 compiler even when launched from an older JVM, and document the Java runtime requirements for building and running computa.jar.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document Computa command loop and collaborators
commitResults.messageBody: Complete JavaDoc coverage for the remaining non-private API and clarify the purpose of Computa's stateful collaborators and parser utility constructor. No runtime behavior is changed.
Computa's deadline and event validation messages exceed the Java style line-length limit. Wrap the message expressions while preserving their user-facing text and behavior.
Capture the SE-EDU intermediate conventions for naming, layout, imports, control flow, line length, and JavaDoc so Java reviews use one project-specific reference.
Capture the SE-EDU subject and body conventions for focused, imperative, readable commit messages that explain what changed and why.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enforce project coding and Git standards
commitResults.messageBody: Require all agents to apply the SE-EDU Java conventions to production and test code and the SE-EDU Git conventions to future commit messages. Reference the project-specific skills as the review entry points.

Users cannot locate a task without scanning the full list.

Add case-insensitive description search with original task numbers and
friendly responses for invalid or unmatched searches. Document the new
behavior and cover it with UI and JUnit tests.
Bring the coding-standard documentation, Java fixes, and project skills into the default branch so the repository enforces the required conventions.
Bring keyword search and its automated coverage into the default branch so the tagged Level 9 feature is available from master.

The UI test plan's 10-second timeout can expire while a clean Java build is still compiling on developer machines.

Increase the documented timeout to 30 seconds so the runner can complete the build before comparing output.
